speaker: narrator
text: Every temple holds a story. Every artifact carries a memory. Protecting heritage means protecting our history.

speaker: aryan
text: I have recovered the bell and conch teaching replica.

speaker: pujari
text: This bell and conch are fictional teaching replicas, not objects removed from Puri. Bells and conches accompany worship and the early morning Mangal Aarti.
note: Fictional teaching replica; historical context sourced in pujari_lore.json

speaker: pujari
text: The present Shree Jagannath Temple began under the Eastern Ganga king Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva in the twelfth century.
note: Fictional teaching replica; historical context sourced in pujari_lore.json

speaker: pujari
text: King Indradyumna and the sacred timber belong to the temple foundation tradition. We distinguish that cherished legend from the history of the present building.
note: Fictional teaching replica; historical context sourced in pujari_lore.json

speaker: pujari
text: Legends express devotion and community identity. Historical claims use inscriptions and other evidence; both deserve careful explanation.
note: Fictional teaching replica; historical context sourced in pujari_lore.json

speaker: aryan
text: I have recovered the palm-leaf teaching manuscript.
note: Fictional teaching replica; historical context sourced in pujari_lore.json

speaker: pujari
text: This fictional manuscript replica introduces Odisha palm-leaf engraving, called tala patra. Craftspeople prepare leaves and incise fine lines with a stylus.
note: Fictional teaching replica; historical context sourced in pujari_lore.json

speaker: pujari
text: Dark pigment makes the engraved lines visible. Palm leaves preserve writing and images through skilled preparation and careful storage.
note: Fictional teaching replica; historical context sourced in pujari_lore.json

speaker: pujari
text: Jayadeva composed the Gita Govinda in the twelfth century. Its devotional poetry is closely associated with Jagannath worship.
note: Fictional teaching replica; historical context sourced in pujari_lore.json

speaker: pujari
text: Manuscripts preserve language, poetry and the knowledge of their makers. Real leaves are fragile and need trained conservation rather than a quick repair.
note: Fictional teaching replica; historical context sourced in pujari_lore.json

speaker: aryan
text: I have recovered the wheel seal and painted teaching medallion.
note: Fictional teaching replica; historical context sourced in pujari_lore.json

speaker: pujari
text: This fictional seal represents the Nilachakra, the sacred metal wheel above the Puri temple. The wheel itself remains on the temple; it is never a collectible.
note: Fictional teaching replica; historical context sourced in pujari_lore.json

speaker: pujari
text: The temple banner is associated with this wheel. We respect that living tradition without presenting tales about the wind as measured science.
note: Fictional teaching replica; historical context sourced in pujari_lore.json

speaker: pujari
text: Odisha Pattachitra artists create detailed narrative paintings. The medallion is our invented teaching design, not an authenticated historic temple object.
note: Fictional teaching replica; historical context sourced in pujari_lore.json

speaker: pujari
text: Pattachitra carries stories through line, colour and patient workshop practice. Supporting practising artists helps skills pass between generations.
note: Fictional teaching replica; historical context sourced in pujari_lore.json

speaker: aryan
text: I have recovered the ceremonial teaching vessel.
note: Fictional teaching replica; historical context sourced in pujari_lore.json

speaker: pujari
text: This brass vessel is a fictional teaching replica. Rohini Kunda is a sacred place within the Puri temple tradition, not a puzzle tank to be disturbed.
note: Fictional teaching replica; historical context sourced in pujari_lore.json

speaker: pujari
text: The temple kitchen prepares offerings in earthen pots. Mahaprasad connects worship, food and a community of cooks, servitors and devotees.
note: Fictional teaching replica; historical context sourced in pujari_lore.json

speaker: pujari
text: Nirmalya includes dried sacred rice cherished by devotees. Our brass replica illustrates heritage learning; it is not an actual kitchen pot or sacred offering.
note: Fictional teaching replica; historical context sourced in pujari_lore.json

speaker: pujari
text: Living heritage includes the people who maintain a tradition. We honour their knowledge and work, and avoid treating sacred food as treasure or a commodity.
note: Fictional teaching replica; historical context sourced in pujari_lore.json

speaker: aryan
text: I have recovered the chariot teaching medallion and banner.
note: Fictional teaching replica; historical context sourced in pujari_lore.json

speaker: pujari
text: This fictional medallion and banner recall Ratha Yatra. The chariots travel along Puri Grand Avenue towards Gundicha Temple.
note: Fictional teaching replica; historical context sourced in pujari_lore.json

speaker: pujari
text: Jagannath rides Nandighosha, Balabhadra rides Taladhwaja, and Subhadra rides Darpadalana. Nandighosha has sixteen wheels.
note: Fictional teaching replica; historical context sourced in pujari_lore.json

speaker: pujari
text: Artisans build the festival chariots anew each year. The celebration brings the deities into public view, expressing a widely shared tradition of devotion.
note: Fictional teaching replica; historical context sourced in pujari_lore.json

speaker: pujari
text: Rebuilding keeps specialist skills alive through practice and transmission. The knowledge of the makers matters as much as the finished woodwork.
note: Fictional teaching replica; historical context sourced in pujari_lore.json

speaker: aryan
text: I have recovered the teaching finial and chronicle ornament.
note: Fictional teaching replica; historical context sourced in pujari_lore.json

speaker: pujari
text: This finial ornament and chronicle are fictional teaching replicas. A kalasha crowns temple architecture; no actual temple crown has been taken in this story.
note: Fictional teaching replica; historical context sourced in pujari_lore.json

speaker: pujari
text: Nabakalebara is the periodic renewal of the wooden sacred images in the Jagannath tradition. Its ritual calendar is not a fixed annual replacement.
note: Fictional teaching replica; historical context sourced in pujari_lore.json

speaker: pujari
text: The sacred images remain untouched in our game. Returning these replicas reminds us that heritage is living community memory, not gold for smugglers.
note: Fictional teaching replica; historical context sourced in pujari_lore.json

speaker: pujari
text: People renew heritage through knowledge, care and shared responsibility. Every temple holds a story; protecting heritage means protecting our history.
